content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze the disease symptoms.

The test image shows two tomato plants. The left plant has dramatic whole-plant wilting - all stems and leaves drooping downward while still somewhat green, in contrast to the healthy right plant. This sudden, complete collapse is highly characteristic of bacterial wilt diseases.

Key visual features:
- Complete plant collapse/wilting
- Leaves still somewhat green (not yellowed first)
- Sudden-onset appearance
- Adjacent healthy plant for comparison

Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt

I'll use my 1 reference image view on Bacterial_Wilt since the sudden collapse is most consistent with Ralstonia solanacearum.

The reference image shows the classic bacterial streaming test for Bacterial_Wilt - a stem cross-section in water with milky bacterial ooze streaming down, and brown vascular discoloration inside the stem. This confirms Ralstonia solanacearum as the pathogen.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: Sudden, complete whole-plant collapse with stems/leaves drooping while still green — no progressive yellowing from bottom up (which would suggest Verticillium_Wilt)
- The rapid onset wilting of the entire plant without yellowing/browning first is the hallmark of Bacterial_Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum)
- The adjacent healthy plant suggests localized soil-borne infection
- Bacterial_Wilt causes vascular blockage that leads to this sudden, catastrophic wilt
